comment.body:
# Milestone 1 — owner-authorised execution plan · 14 November 2026

**Status: authorised and starting. This comment records the owner's explicit approval in the archaeology conversation on 14 November 2026.**

> “record plan in git issues then **Proceed with Milestone 1 investigation and knowledge capture under the prepared brief, including one isolated capture branch and one Draft/HOLD PR. Keep merge, successor issue creation, historical retirement, broad documentation rewriting and implementation for their separate approval gates.**”

This is the phase-specific go-ahead required by #571. The original issue and M0 snapshot remain intact. This comment records the authorised plan; it does not create a canonical successor engineering issue.

**Programme:** [techrote/cybersand issue #571](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/issues/571).

**Evidence baseline:** [Complete Milestone 0 report and frozen inventory](https://chatgpt.com/library?file_id=libfile_c4eba0d4449881919b03a7c5e2204ddf&account_id=personal).

This record transfers the owner's direct clarifications and the agreed bounded execution package. The complete capture will be proposed on one isolated branch in one Draft/HOLD PR; the original source records remain intact.

The M0 baseline was 14 November 2026 at 00:29:51 UTC: accepted main `ac0d9fb944cb5a81369d03c0c3bc5eab50ab6742`, 92 open issues and 179 open PRs. Those are baseline counts, not a claim about the state when M1 begins. M1 must refresh current main, open records and active PR heads, retaining changes in a separate delta record.

## 1. Owner intent now available for assessment

**Primary provenance:** the owner's clarification messages in this conversation on 14 November 2026. The summaries below should later be transferred with that provenance, preserving the distinction between confirmed intent and an exploratory suggestion. They are not a line-by-line approval of every historical document.

| Topic | Confirmed intent or carefully scoped interpretation |
|---|---|
| Product direction | #534 broadly matches the owner's intent. CyberSand is a paint-and-play engine as an authoring system, centred on Workbench. Detailed historical wording still requires reconciliation. |
| Creative controls | Easy-to-learn access to many controls, mechanical modifiers and modulators, with deeper access available when desired. Painting should grow toward the range between classic MSPaint and GIMP/Krita. |
| Physical character | “convincing>consistent.” Authored effects, approximations and selectable alternatives are desirable for appearance, feel, feasibility, performance and interesting behaviour. This is a product principle, not retroactive qualification of failed experiments. |
| Development feedback | Continue building and evaluating actual authored scenes. Human judgement of feel should drive tuning. Scientific parameter sweeps are not an adequate substitute for representative play. Correctness and targeted performance checks retain their appropriate roles. |
| Agent authoring | Current envisaged roles include conversational autofill, feature/flavour/item generation and tiny/local models for greebles, texturing and randomness. These are desired roles, not permanent claims about particular model capabilities. |
| Actors and game structure | NPC controllers, Rapier actors and drone work should be revisited soon. Keep the engine flexible across passive exhibits, flight environments, digging games and other experiments. Game-facing scoring and consequential combat damage wait until the arrangements and actors are fun. |
| Workbench convergence | Valuable tools and capabilities should become compatible with and accessible through Workbench, serving as an ergonomic creative, development, control and monitoring environment. This does not require identical internal ownership for every specialist tool. |
| Destructible structures | Desired outcomes include blasting/cutting coherent pieces loose and having them roll or topple. Full structural-integrity analysis is not a prerequisite. Prepared chunk sizes and declared break conditions are a promising owner-suggested avenue; the exact mechanism remains to be investigated. |
| Materials Lab | The owner wanted easy modification and audition, especially changing values from a Workbench window for dynamic/custom trials. Isolated comparison tools are appreciated but do not satisfy that whole interaction. |
| Strata Theatre | Four-layer presentation should be an available Workbench option. Historical exclusions represent scope boundaries, not an enduring rejection of the capability. |
| Save and Flatten | Save preserves the desired layout without unexpectedly destroying live Undo. Maps need not always be flattened. Explicit Flatten provides a material-only baseline and discards burdensome construction history. |
| Compatibility | Do not promise extensive preservation of every old project's behaviour. A material-only Flatten fallback can recover useful layout in newer versions. Exact identity mapping and container mechanics remain engineering details. |
| World scale | Fixed canvases plus persistent areas should cover most desired uses. Broad continuous canvases should accommodate biomes or small towns, with later methods to obscure boundaries. “Move away from 1:1 canvases” is interpreted here as allowing non-square/broad layouts; it is not a decision about render-pixel scaling. |
| Distant activity | Simulate a useful border around the viewport or activity, potentially biased toward player movement. Approximate catch-up during a return transition is preferable to conspicuously frozen rooms. |
| Time and transitions | Use game time. A few seconds of transition occasionally is acceptable. An optional deliberate “simulate ahead” control is desired. These are product requirements for future refinement, not implementation tasks launched by this addendum. |
| Abandoned attempts | Discontinuation may reflect disappointing results, a better concurrent approach, supporting work landing elsewhere, staleness or changed short-term priorities. It does not itself reject the underlying idea. Reconstruct the specific reason when evidence allows. |

### Matters that remain engineering work

Exact catch-up approximations, retained simulation state, checkpoint formats, safe runtime material application, prepared-fracture mechanics, layer integration, activity margins and concrete canvas dimensions remain open. The owner should not need to choose these merely to complete the archive.

Some product details can wait for a concrete successor brief: cross-area physical exchanges, which tools need live versus isolated application, and the qualification matrix for a particular experience. They need not block full archaeology.

### How these clarifications change historical assessment

- Use current owner intent to assess relevance; retain the original rationale and outcome as historical evidence.
- Do not turn an old test fixture, temporary capacity, chosen representation or narrow implementation scope into a permanent product requirement.
- Do not infer that a failed experiment now passes because the product priorities changed.
- Distinguish source availability, demonstrated behaviour, qualification, adoption and present desirability.
- A discontinued attempt needs a concise retrospective: purpose, result, stopping reason, surviving value and successor. If the stopping reason cannot be established, say so.
- Preserve worthwhile discoveries outside the current priority themes without automatically creating active obligations for them.

## 2. The authorised Milestone 1 package

**Agreed delivery:** one isolated capture branch and one **Draft/HOLD PR** based on main as refreshed at execution start. It remains unmerged for owner review. One lead investigator coordinates three bounded research lanes; researchers return evidence packets, while the lead maintains shared records and the capture branch.

### Authorised permissions

The owner's approval authorises M1 to:

- Read all relevant repository/GitHub history and inspect existing source, diffs, tests, logs and discussions.
- Refresh the baseline, record deltas and identify protected active development.
- Capture recoverable original evidence and integrity metadata, including expiring artifacts.
- Create the agreed historical index, coverage and finding records on the isolated capture branch.
- Add a separate owner-intent record containing the clarified decisions and their provenance.
- Make the minimum archive-exclusion/validation changes required for initial historical retrieval isolation.
- Open and update the single Draft/HOLD capture PR and return the M1 report.

### Reserved actions

The package does not authorise engine implementation, restarting old branches, changing active implementation branches, merging the capture PR, creating canonical successor issues, editing/commenting on/closing historical tickets, relabelling, deleting branches or artifacts, broad documentation rewriting, benchmark campaigns or scheduled workers.

Normal investigation does not need repeated permission for each family. A new expensive experiment, unavailable evidence requiring another access path, or a material change to this scope should be surfaced specifically.

## 3. M1 execution: three concrete work packages

### Package A — Scope, protection, authority separation and vulnerable evidence

**Work**

1. Refresh accepted main, open items, active PR heads and explicit custody records. Keep the M0 snapshot intact; record later changes separately.
2. Account individually for the 271 baseline open records. Include metadata for the related closed reference universe and follow closed history wherever it materially informs a live family.
3. Mark active development as protected. Inventory inclusion is not retirement eligibility.
4. Prepare effective historical isolation before the new archive enters any default retrieval path.
5. Preserve expiring original evidence first. The M0 investigation identified MAT-003 artifact [12468697797](https://github.com/techrote/cybersand/actions/runs/39876455400/artifacts/12468697797), advertised then with expiry 22 November 2026 at 00:13:13 UTC. Recheck availability, fetch where accessible, verify bytes and hash, and record any gap honestly.
6. Transfer the owner's clarifications into their separate proposed record, with date, source, scope and uncertainty.

**Exit**

A complete scope/protection ledger, explicit delta handling, a separate owner-intent record, an actual recoverability manifest and verified initial archive isolation. A URL alone does not count as captured evidence.

### Package B — Complete the family investigations

Use the twelve M0 queues as an initial partition and the nine pilots as starting evidence. Do not restart completed research unnecessarily, and do not mistake a pilot summary for assessment of every item in its queue.

| Research lane | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Simulation and material behaviour | Soliding, contact, liquids, material semantics and physical/performance experiments |
| State, persistence and authoring data | Carriers, epochs, durable edits, residency, generation, saves and Flatten history |
| Runtime and creative composition | Actors, equipment, Workbench integration, rendering, layered presentation, agents and transport |

The lead handles cross-family reconciliation, governance and current-intent provenance, assigning specialised recording/diagnostic work to the relevant lane. Balance the lanes using small lineage-based packets, not fixed ownership of enormous topic lists.

Each item has one primary family. Cross-family findings are linked, not re-investigated independently. Distinguish relationships such as stacked-on, adopted-via, superseded-by and qualified-against; Git ancestry alone does not prove semantic adoption.

For every family, apply all twelve #571 dimensions. For every individual item, record justified depth and separate dispositions for its ticket, idea, implementation and technical evidence. Deeper code/test tracing is required where an adoption, salvage, correctness or negative-result claim depends on it.

**Exit**

Every in-scope historical open item has a justified assessment state and depth; important closed relationships have been followed; recoverable value and doctrine claims have traceable findings; unresolved matters are explicit.

### Package C — Challenge conclusions and prepare synthesis

Independently review:

- High-risk doctrine judgments and claims of current owner authority.
- “Already satisfied” findings against actual successor semantics.
- Valuable implementation/test salvage and hidden integration costs.
- A sample of “no further value” dispositions.
- Artifact recoverability and the separation of original results from later interpretation.
- Cross-family overlaps and active-work protection.

A transfer receipt should connect:

**Source claim or asset → disposition → destination → verification method → remaining limitation.**

Destinations may be an archive record, code/test/artifact reference, current decision, proposed opportunity or a justified no-further-action conclusion. There need not be a new issue for every old ticket.

**Exit**

Return an auditable M1 capture PR and a compact synthesis report: coverage, recovered knowledge, unresolved evidence, doctrine changes, contextual owner questions and candidate thematic opportunities. Do not create the successor issues or perform retirement at this stage.

## 4. Lightweight records and effective isolation

Use a small number of maintained sources:

- Historical family notes and generated navigation under a proposed `docs/history/engineering/`.
- One item ledger, retaining separate coverage, assessment, transfer and retirement states.
- One typed findings store supplying salvage, negative-result and doctrine views.
- A distinct owner-intent/decision record, following the repository's decision conventions.
- Evidence copies with source/executed identities, original verdicts, hashes, actual capture status and recovery references. Keep bulky originals out of the main code tree.

Do not duplicate the same finding across six hand-maintained registries. Use short meaningful records and generate views where useful.

Historical material must receive an explicit non-authoritative envelope. Imported words such as “Approved,” “Current” and “must” remain quoted historical source status. They cannot override the archive's authority class.

Keep the archive out of default coding/RAG inputs through explicit corpus/ingestion controls, including automatic link expansion and metadata after chunking. Confirm deliberate historical search still works. Broader documentation/RAG reconciliation remains a separate later programme.

The current owner-intent record is a different authority class; it is not buried inside the historical archive or silently manufactured from implementation details.

## 5. After M1: the remaining gates

| Phase | Outcome | Owner gate |
|---|---|---|
| **M1 review** | Inspect the capture PR, evidence, gaps and synthesis | Accept/request refinement; merge only with explicit approval |
| **M2 reconciliation and canonical synthesis** | Discuss a small set of coherent opportunities and any newly discovered material contradictions | Approve actual new issue text before creation; avoid duplicating active work |
| **M3 verified retirement** | Refresh active state; verify transfers; present itemised closure batches and proposed disposition text | Approve the concrete batch; no branch deletion or old-code merge as a side effect |
| **Separate Markdown/RAG reconciliation** | Reconcile current claims using historical evidence and owner decisions; test actual retrieval behaviour | Approve a separate programme; initial archive containment already exists |
| **M4 issue-level execution** | Revisit one new issue against then-current source, active work, alternatives and desired experience | Refine and authorise that issue individually before fresh implementation |

### Candidate synthesis themes

Current owner direction suggests Workbench access/continuity, actor and equipment composition, live material audition, Strata presentation, prepared destruction and authoring/persistence as strong areas to examine. They are **assessment lenses**, not a preselected implementation backlog. The archaeology may discover additional valuable work or establish that an existing active effort already covers a need.

### What the owner should receive at M1 completion

- A single reviewable Draft/HOLD capture PR.
- Complete individual coverage with honest depth and unresolved states.
- A concise index of recovered ideas, code, tests and negative findings.
- A doctrine register with scope, rationale and supersession.
- The separate owner-intent record, including these clarifications.
- A recoverability report identifying actual captured originals and remaining losses/gaps.
- A short opportunity synthesis for M2, and only genuinely new contextual questions.
- A protection/delta report demonstrating that active development has not been disturbed.

### Execution and next gate

The refreshed intake still has accepted main `ac0d9fb944cb5a81369d03c0c3bc5eab50ab6742`, with **93 open issues and 181 open PRs** before creating the capture PR. The three additions beyond M0 (#580, #581, #582) will be recorded as deltas and protected while their active scope is assessed. This is not a blanket development freeze.

One lead investigator maintains the shared ledger and capture branch. Three read-only research lanes return evidence packets; no scheduled workers or implementation tasks are launched. Completion will be reported here and in the single Draft/HOLD capture PR, including actual coverage, validation, evidence gaps and the next review gate. **No merge is authorised.**
